newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League club Essendon is planning an aggressive recruiting strategy in the lead-up to the national draft on October 31. The club is in danger of losing up to seven players including captain Gary O'Donnell. Page 22.

The announcement of joint moratorium on signing players until the end of August by the Australian Rugby League and Super League has been described as premature and disappointing by ARL chief executive Neil Whittaker. Whittaker has said that he wanted to discuss the proposal with clubs first before it became public. Page 22.

Australian tennis player Todd Woodbridge is the sole Australian survivor in the Wimbledon singles quarter finals despite many commentators predicting fellow Australian players Pat Rafter and Mark Philippoussis to be title contenders. Woodbridge defeated Rafter yesterday despite their match being delayed twice by rain. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League team North Sydney is considering a move to Gosford to avoid the likely merger of the Bears with rival Manly-Warringah if the Australian Rugby League and Super League agree to merge next year. If the move proceeds, Gosford Council is expected to build a multi-sports stadium and the Central Coast Leagues Club could link up with the club. Page 54.

After Australian Rugby Union test second-rower David Giffin broke his foot, little-known Queensland player Matthew Cockbain has been selected for the Bledisloe Cup series between Australia and New Zealand. Cockbain's selection has come as a surprise as he only began playing representative football a few months ago in the Super 12 series. Page 54.

The weather forecast in Manchester for the upcoming Ashes cricket match between Australia and England at Old Trafford is for further showers. The wet conditions suit the English team with Australian captain Mark Taylor describing the wicket as slow. Page 4.
THE AGE

The sudden departure of Danny Corcoran from Australian Football League team Essendon is likely to result in court action with allegations being made that documents were removed from the club days before Corcoran's departure for the Melbourne Demons club. Essendon says they would consider releasing Corcoran to Melbourne if the missing documents were returned. Page B8.

Sri Lankan test cricketer Asanka Gurusinha has been granted permanent residency in Australia and is keen to represent Victoria in the Sheffield Shield competition this year. Gurusinha came to Australia after a disagreement with the Sri Lankan cricket board over selection last year, but has sparked controversy here over the merits of selecting players for state sides who are not eligible to represent the Australian team. Page B6.

Australian Football League club Collingwood is expected to allow Aaron James to play in reserve grade this weekend after the club had suspended him indefinitely for an incident involving alcohol last month. James has not played for the Collingwood since round 11 and it is unclear if the club will retain him if the charges are proven. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Former Australian cricket captain Allan Border has predicted that Victorian player Matthew Elliott will save the Ashes series against England for Australia. Border has described Elliott as being destined to become one of the game's exceptional players. Pae 96.

Australian Football League team North Melbourne has announced that star player Corey McKernan will have knee surgery at the end of the season. McKernan has been battling with the injury since last years preliminary round against Brisbane, and re-injured it during this years opening round against Melbourne. Page 94.

The signing of Collingwood Warriors Goran Lozanovski and Con Boutsianis to the South Melbourne Soccer club has been described as a coup for coach Ange Postecoglou. In other transfer negotiations, the club lost defender Alex Kuzmanovic to West Adelaide. Page 89.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The New South Wales Rugby Union will shortly hand out 'report cards' to clubs to give them an indication of their likelihood of being relegated next year. The union plans to reduce the premiership next year by two clubs in a bid to raise the standard of play in the AAMI Cup. Page 95.

This weekend Australian Football League player Mark Bayes will attract attention as the only Sydney Swans player to have won a match in Perth when the team travels west to play Fremantle. Bayes had previously been known as the only Sydney Swans player to have contested a final as a Swan before the team reached the Grand Final last year. Page 86.

The 'battling trainers' of the Canterbury race-course have attracted the support of three of Canterbury's most prominent councillors and put the Sydney Turf Club's night racing plans in doubt. The trainers are fighting the closure of Canterbury Park as a training centre. Page 94.
